integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action cinematic drama, 2.39:1 anamorphic composition inside a dim hotel bar at night. The camera slowly trucks behind foreground wine glasses, revealing an elegant woman with a cool, restrained voice (S1) sitting alone at the counter. In the mirror behind her, a man with a low British voice (S2) quietly approaches. Without turning around, she notices his reflection. He stops behind her and says: <d>[English] You still order the same thing.</d> [Shot 2] At 00:05.000, the camera cuts to her reflection in a tight mirror close-up. She rotates the glass once and replies: <d>[English] You still arrive too late.</d> [Shot 3] At 00:09.000, a reverse close-up frames the man as his confident expression briefly collapses. He asks: <d>[English] Is there still time?</d> [Shot 4] At 00:12.000, the camera cuts back to the woman. She finally turns toward him and answers: <d>[English] Sit down.</d> Hold on their silent eye contact. Accurate English lip synchronization, restrained micro-expressions, correct eyelines, mirror reflections, shallow depth of field, subtle anamorphic flare, fine 35mm grain, no subtitles or readable labels.

overall_soundscape: Low bar ambience, ice moving inside a glass, distant traffic, quiet footsteps and the soft scrape of a bar stool.

non_diegetic_music: Sparse upright-bass notes and muted piano chords at a slow tempo.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action cinematic scene, one continuous 15-second surfing shot shortly after sunrise on a quiet, realistic coastline. The sky is pale and slightly overcast near the horizon, while a narrow opening between the clouds allows low warm sunlight to travel horizontally across the ocean. The deeper water remains restrained steel blue, the shadowed wave face appears dark blue-green, and only the thin crest and suspended spray receive pale golden backlight. No tropical postcard colors, spectators, buildings, boats, or commercial beach imagery.

A 24-year-old Polynesian woman with an athletic build and long wet dark hair wears a plain charcoal-black full-body wetsuit. She rides a slightly weathered pale-yellow shortboard with no visible branding. Her identity, facial features, skin tone, body proportions, wetsuit, surfboard, fins, and ankle leash remain stable throughout the shot.

The camera begins at water level in a natural 65mm side Tracking Shot, moving parallel to the surfer at matching speed. She is already standing and traveling diagonally across the lower face of a clean rising wave. The low sun remains behind the wave, leaving her face partially in cool shadow while creating a narrow warm rim of light around her wet hair, shoulders, forearms, and the edge of the surfboard.

She bends both knees and enters one controlled bottom turn. Her rear foot applies pressure over the fins while the inside rail cuts into the dark water. A restrained arc of spray rises behind the board. Each droplet briefly catches the backlight before falling naturally. The camera moves slightly closer without changing sides or losing the complete surfboard.

The wave begins folding above her. She redirects upward, lowers her torso, and enters a short naturally forming barrel. As the translucent wall of water moves between her and the rising sun, the light changes gradually from cool steel blue to luminous turquoise and muted sea green. Moving bands of refracted sunlight travel across her face, wetsuit, hands, and board. The exposure adjusts smoothly without sudden brightness changes.

Inside the barrel, she remains in a low balanced stance. Her front hand stays near the open exit while her rear hand extends lightly toward the moving wall of water without touching it. The wave lip passes overhead with realistic thickness and speed. Her wet hair responds naturally to airflow and water droplets; it never changes length or shape.

The barrel begins narrowing. She shifts pressure through her rear foot and makes one compact directional correction toward the opening. White water briefly surrounds the tail of the board, but her body, legs, feet, board, and leash remain clearly continuous. She accelerates through the illuminated spray and exits the barrel upright.

As she emerges, the low sunlight reaches her face for the first time. Warm amber light travels across her wet cheek, eyelashes, and the upper surface of the pale-yellow board while the ocean behind her remains cool blue. She rises slightly from the crouch, releases a held breath, and a small spontaneous smile appears. The camera gradually loses speed, allowing her to glide ahead through a trail of softly backlit spray during the final three seconds.

ARRI Alexa 35 aesthetic, 2.39:1, natural 65mm water-level photography, restrained cinematic contrast, cool steel-blue shadows balanced by pale amber sunrise highlights, translucent turquoise water without excessive saturation, realistic changing exposure, subtle halation around backlit spray, natural wet skin, soft highlight roll-off, deep but readable shadow detail, physically accurate wave formation, correct surfboard buoyancy, precise foot placement, natural balance, realistic water interaction, restrained motion blur, and fine organic film grain. No enormous fantasy wave, no aerial stunt, no wipeout, no artificial spotlight, no heavy orange grading, no teal-orange blockbuster grading, no artificial HDR, no excessive lens flare, no beauty-commercial skin, no changing surfboard, no detached leash, no duplicated body parts, no floating feet, no subtitles, no captions, and no readable text.

overall_soundscape: The broad movement of the ocean surrounds the sharper hiss of the surfboard rail cutting across the wave. The sound becomes briefly enclosed and resonant inside the barrel, followed by a fuller release of breaking water and the surfer's controlled breath as she emerges.

non_diegetic_music: A low sustained cello note and sparse muted percussion begin beneath the approach. The percussion disappears inside the barrel, then a soft electric-guitar chord enters when sunlight reaches her face.
